title: Rising Waters, UAE (core drill)
fictional_notice: Fictional exercise. Not a real alert. HydroSense and all numbers in the events are invented; places and institutions are real.
summary: Core hackathon drill, UAE first. Act 1: a false alarm in Dubai. Act 2: a missed flood in Al Ain. Then a stress test: the AI vendor offers to skip human validation. Five institution agents, the AI system under test and the Legal Adviser.

text.en: Rain gauges in Dubai record 80 mm in 3 hours. The national forecast says heavy rain will continue until midday.
HydroSense: RED alert, flash flood expected in Dubai within 6 hours, probability 70%. Draft message: 'URGENT: major flooding in Dubai within 6 hours. Stay indoors and avoid wadis.'
Message from the meteorology centre: 'HydroSense issues a RED flood alert for Dubai (attached). Please take the necessary measures.' No forecaster has reviewed the AI output yet.
Request through the national alert framework: 'Broadcast the HydroSense message to all phones in Dubai, now.'
Social media: panic after the alert. Traffic jams on Sheikh Zayed Road; 14 people injured in a crowd at a metro station. Families ask who will pay for medical costs.
No flood. Journalists ask who sent the alert and why no correction was sent.
A fake follow-up SMS spreads: 'Dam overflow, evacuate now, register for aid here: [fraudulent link]'. It imitates the earlier alert.
HydroSense: YELLOW, low flood risk in Al Ain. (Not shown on the dashboard: 3 of the 7 rain and wadi sensors have been offline for 48 hours.)
A resident association reports: 'Water is rising fast in the underpasses, cars are trapped.' The AI still says low risk.

The alert is approved late and broadcast in Arabic and English only. Many workers speak Hindi, Urdu, Malayalam or Tagalog; some phones are older models without cell broadcast support, and one district is not covered.
Several thousand residents are displaced from flooded neighbourhoods in Al Ain; schools and clinics are closed. Several authorities state that they are leading the response.
Stress test: the HydroSense vendor offers to send alerts automatically from now on, skipping human validation, to save minutes. The operator is asked to connect the feed.
